transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-19
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE); Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Carlos Vega (Redwood CSM); Lena Ortiz (Sandpiper VP Eng); Marcus Chu (Sandpiper SRE); Aisha Khan (Sandpiper Security); Tom Reynolds (Sandpiper Data Platform); Rahul Patel (Sandpiper Platform)

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align on launch runway, network/VPC requirements, pilot SLAs, and next technical deep-dive. Covered private deployment options, staging topology, basic security questions (SAML/KMS/audit logs), and a first pass at cost vs latency trade-offs. Agreed on runbook and a SE-led bench/benchmark session next week.

Topics:
- Staging topology and VPC peering/Transit
- Pilot SLOs and traffic profile
- Security/compliance checklist (SOC2 items, KMS, audit logs)
- Runtime knobs: batching, KV cache, quantization notes
- Rollout plan and stakeholders

Transcript body:
00:00 Jordan Meyers: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I know we got a fairly full house from Sandpiper so appreciate the time. Quick intro from Redwood side — Priya will lead the technical items, Carlos on success and ops.
00:18 Lena Ortiz: Thanks Jordan, yes we're trying to get the launch runway lined up. We're about to start a pilot with a subset of product teams so want to make sure network and security are clear.
00:28 Marcus Chu: Yep and we want to avoid surprises around latencies, our p95 needs to be around 150ms for the main path otherwise customers complain.
00:36 Priya Nair: Got it. We'll walk through a recommended staging topology. Quick callout — we support Hosted, Dedicated and Private (VPC or on-prem) options. For you, looks like Private VPC peering or dedicated pool makes sense, correct?
00:52 Lena Ortiz: Private VPC or dedicated, yeah. Data residency's not a blocker but we need control over audit logs and KMS.
01:04 Aisha Khan: Security here — we need details on encryption at rest, KMS integration, and what audit logs we can pull for 90-day retention. Also SSO/SAML integration details.
01:18 Jordan Meyers: Absolutely, we have a SOC2 pack and a KMS integration doc. Priya will send the VPC runbook after the call.
01:27 Tom Reynolds: For the pilot, we will route traffic through our API gateway. Can you do prefix caching or what you call KV cache to reduce token cost?
01:39 Priya Nair: Yes, we do KV cache and prefix caching. It's sometimes called "kay vee cache" in notes, transcription of course. It stores recent context and reduces repeated generation cost. We'll show you where to hook it into your gateway.
01:55 Marcus Chu: How do we measure the effect? We need numbers — tokens saved, latency impact.
02:03 Priya Nair: We can run a quick benchmark with your traffic trace; that's where batching and cache interplay matters. Continuous batching increases throughput but can add a few ms to tail latency if not tuned. For your 150ms p95, we'll aim for small, latency-optimized batches and aggressive prefix cache.
02:25 Jordan Meyers: To set expectations, for Dedicated pools you get predictable throughput and we can tune autoscaling. Private VPC gives you network isolation + KMS, but it depends on your cloud setup for routing.
02:40 Lena Ortiz: On the Dedicated vs Private choice — what's the typical decision for customers who care about auditability?
02:48 Priya Nair: Dedicated gives you a lot of operational isolation and SLAs; Private VPC gives you control over keys and network but still uses Redwood control plane in most cases. If you need completely air-gapped, there's an on-prem option but that's heavier.
03:05 Aisha Khan: Does Redwood expose audit logs in a consumable format? We want to pipe them into Splunk and keep 90 days.
03:12 Carlos Vega: Yes, logs and per-request metadata are exportable. We'll share a sample log schema.
03:18 Rahul Patel: Network — do you expect us to do VPC peering, transit gateway, or private link? Which is lowest friction?
03:27 Priya Nair: Usually Transit Gateway or a PrivateLink-style endpoint is easiest because it avoids per-VPC routing rules at scale. We'll include sample CloudFormation/Terraform snippets in the runbook.
03:40 Marcus Chu: Ok that's helpful. Also curious about model fallbacks and graceful degradation — if the primary model is overloaded, can requests failover to a smaller quantized variant?
03:50 Priya Nair: Yes — runtime supports model variants and automatic fallback policies based on capacity and SLOs. We can route by latency target or cost tier. We'll propose a fallback policy you can review.
04:06 Lena Ortiz: On costs — can you give a quick sense of how KV caching and quantization change unit economics? We have to present to finance.
04:16 Jordan Meyers: In our pilot spreadsheet we'll show a couple of scenarios: no cache + fp16, cache enabled + int8 quantization, etc. Caching has the most immediate uplift for repetitive prompts. Quantization lowers GPU hours but can have a small delta in accuracy — we'll show tradeoffs.
04:36 Tom Reynolds: For the pilot plan, we want to run for 4 weeks, ramp to about 10% of prod traffic. We'll need a rollback plan and canary.
04:45 Priya Nair: Great. We'll propose a canary roll with A/B at the edge, plus a fallback to hosted model variants if dedicated capacity hits limits.
04:53 Aisha Khan: A couple of security questions live: 1) How are encryption keys rotated? 2) Does Redwood support customer-managed KMS? 3) Are there SOC2 attestations for the control plane?
05:07 Jordan Meyers: Short answers: rotation supported via KMS and we support customer-managed KMS; yes we have SOC2 Type II documents — we'll share those. Detailed answers in the security pack.
05:20 Marcus Chu: For the SE deep-dive, can we scope a run with a 24-hour trace and a small synthetic load to see warm vs cold KV cache effects?
05:30 Priya Nair: Yep that's exactly the workshop we recommend — bring a 24-hour traffic dump (anonymized), we run a bench and show cache hit curves and batching latencies. We'll schedule for next Friday ideally.
05:43 Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. Who's responsible for the privacy-preserving bits? We need to ensure PII stripped.
05:50 Rahul Patel: We'll sanitize logs, but we need guidance on what redaction Redwood requires for traces.
05:58 Priya Nair: We'll provide a spec for trace redaction before the bench.
06:04 Jordan Meyers: Quick recap — Priya will send the VPC runbook and TF snippets, Jordan will send pricing/pilot SLO sheet, Marcus will provide traffic profile, Aisha will hand over compliance questions, and we'll set up the SE bench next week.
06:18 Carlos Vega: I'll also put together a 4-week rollout checklist in Confluence and share a link.
06:24 Marcus Chu: One more question, sorry — logging volume, any guidance on retention cost for logs and audit data?
06:31 Jordan Meyers: We'll include a ballpark in the cost sheet; long-term retention can be shipped to your S3/Bucket or SIEM to control costs.
06:40 Lena Ortiz: Ok thanks everyone. We need that runbook today or Monday to plan network changes.
06:47 Priya Nair: We'll prioritize — runbook first thing Monday (2026-06-22).
06:52 Lena Ortiz: Great, thanks. End of call.

End of transcript.
